newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saab says profit may be 18 months away.
newsitem.headline: Saab says profit may be 18 months away.

text.p: Swedish carmaker Saab Automobile will not break even this year and may not make a profit in 1997, Saab CEO Robert Hendry told Reuters in an interview on Monday.
"We will not reach breakeven this year. There is also a question about next year. Profit may be 18 months away," Hendry said.
In the first half year of 1996 Saab Automobile showed a loss of 428 million Swedish crowns ($64.6 million) compared to a profit of 195 million for the first half of 1995. ($ = 6.626 Swedish Crowns)

"Our results are weighed down by big investments in product development at the moment. Also the strengthened Swedish currency has hurt us this year and the development of the Swedish krona will be critical to Saab's profitability in the future," Hendry said.

At the same time Hendry warned against pressing for short term gains. "We must be investing in the future. To put short term gains at the top of the list is going about things in the wrong way," Hendry said.
